_metadata.description: Health-guidance evidence: what health authorities say about intake, as opposed to what regulators have prohibited. This is the first evidence in the corpus that is not an enforcement action, and it exists because a risk scale that can only see enforcement reports "no restrictions found" for sugar and for trans fat alike. REVIEW STATUS: ai_seeded. Sources, dates and determinations are real and named; the statements are accurate representations rather than verified verbatim extracts, and carry no URL — a guessed link is worse than none. Replacing these with verbatim text pulled from the published documents is a curation task, not a code change.

records.threshold: under 10% of total energy intake, ideally under 5%
records.statement: WHO recommends reducing the intake of free sugars to less than 10% of total energy intake, and suggests a further reduction to below 5%. Free sugars include sugars added to foods by the manufacturer, cook or consumer, plus sugars naturally present in honey, syrups and fruit juices.

citation.title: Guideline: Sugars intake for adults and children

records.statement: WHO calls for the elimination of industrially-produced trans-fatty acids from the global food supply. Partially hydrogenated oils are their principal source. Trans-fat intake is associated with increased risk of coronary heart disease.

citation.title: REPLACE: An action package to eliminate industrially-produced trans-fatty acids

records.statement: FDA determined that partially hydrogenated oils are no longer Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) for any use in human food.

citation.title: Final Determination Regarding Partially Hydrogenated Oils

records.statement: JECFA has allocated Citric acid an ADI "not specified" — the designation used when a substance is of very low toxicity and its intake at the levels needed to achieve the desired technological effect does not represent a hazard to health.

citation.org: Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives
citation.title: Evaluations of the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives (JECFA)
